newsitem.title: UK: Gold sidelined by focus on strong stock market.
newsitem.headline: Gold sidelined by focus on strong stock market.

text.p: Gold prices were likely to remain compressed in a narrow band on Tuesday as the spotlight firmly turned to surging stock markets, dealers said.
"The big players are focusing on the Dow, making hay while the sun shines. People are waiting until something changes in the precious metals," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed slightly firmer at $383.30 an ounce, compared to $382.80 on Monday morning and $382.65 in the afternoon.
But prices were likely to hold in the $382-$385 area, despite breaking above a three-week-old downtrend line after closing firmer in New York on Monday, dealers and analysts said.
"Initial support at $382 should hold gold now and downside for silver and platinum looks slim near term," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
"But none of these precious metals looks likely to enjoy any corrective gains worth talking about," she added.
Trading volumes were thin with big players concentrating on surging stocks, dealers said.

The FTSE 100-share index hit a new high of 3,986.7 points in early trading after Wall Street racked up a record close on Monday, fuelled by growing hopes that U.S. interest rates would remain unchanged.
The bullion market was still awaiting a decision by the International Monetary Fund on a controversial plan to sell five million ounces of gold to finance aid to poor countries.
International monetary sources said the IMF, due to resume discussion on Wednesday, was having trouble reaching agreement.
"The IMF is teasing us," a dealer said. The protracted debate has undermined prices in recent days, but dealers expect that a decision could lead to a brisk, if short-term, rally.
The white industrial metals were slightly firmer, but dealers said they should be doing better considering the strong performance of the stock market.
Silver was up just two cents from Monday's London close at $5.07 an ounce, dragged down by sluggishness in gold and weakness in the other white metals platinum and palladium.
Palladium was hovering near three-year lows at around $121.75 an ounce, and was vulnerable to further losses, dealers said. Platinum was up nearly $1 at $388.50.
